spec_match.rationale: Queries the real 'local-network' permission name via permissions.query(), explains why the grant must pre-exist for worker-initiated fetches, and maps each state to concrete background-fetch behaviour.

interactive.rationale: Auto-queries on load with a re-query button, and the comparison table queries several real permission names live rather than hard-coding states.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The card promises query-before-you-register guidance driven by the actual state, which the page delivers.

edge_cases.rationale: The unrecognised-name TypeError is treated as a first-class informative state ('a browser that cannot answer is one whose background fetch will not have a grant'), not an error path.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6225598451154944 and the Local Network Access specification.

conformance.rationale: The queryable/does-not-prompt assertions match this page and honestly fail pre-154, but the suite's background-fetch-requires-user-activation assertion fails on fresh profiles for state reasons (no service worker registration) — flagged for a human, not edited.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): the query honestly reported 'local-network' as not a valid PermissionName with the full TypeError, and the comparison table returned live states (geolocation/notifications prompt, background-sync granted); console clean, screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and logs the queried state.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables, captioned tables, state as text, no static card.

accessibility.rationale: aria-live detail, captioned tables with scoped headers, single labelled 44px button.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read).

openQuestions.title: Truncate or wrap the raw TypeError in the state banner
openQuestions.detail: On a pre-154 build the #state banner renders the full 200-plus-character TypeError string ('Failed to read the name property from PermissionDescriptor...'). It is honest, but the key fact — 'local-network is not a recognised permission name here' — is buried in parser prose. Lead with the plain-language state and put the raw error in a smaller mono line or a details element.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/local-network-access-restrictions-for-background-fetch/permission-state/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp), where 'local-network' is not yet a valid PermissionName. The page treats that TypeError as informative signal, exactly as it should, and its comparison table proves the query machinery works by returning live states for real permission names on the same origin. Console/network clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact; desktop and mobile screenshots read with no overflow; /conformance/ ran 4 pass / 3 fail (two honest pre-154 fails plus the flagged fresh-profile user-activation assertion). One minor presentation follow-up for the raw error text.
